clarifications.observation: The new AC-02 requires resume to go to the current live moment. But current behavior on all platforms (iOS, Android, web-desktop) is resume-from-paused-position.

clarifications.answer: PM: 'On resume, the stream starts from the current live moment, not the previous paused position'. iOS developer: 'Confirmed — iOS can jump to the live moment on resume. It lands very close to live but slightly behind (a few seconds of recent footage), due to normal live-stream buffering. Expected behavior, same on all platforms.', Android developer: 'Same with iOS. Due to normal live-stream buffering, it can land very close to live but this is expected.',

resolution.rationale: Confirmed as the intended NEW behaviour on all platforms (PM 68319; iOS 68306; Android 68316). IMPORTANT test tolerance: resume lands very close to live but a few seconds behind due to normal live buffering — that is expected, not a defect (do not assert exact-live). This is a behaviour change vs the current product, so it must be implemented and tested anew on every platform.

clarifications.source: NEWLY SURFACED on 2026-07-08 sync — AC-03 vs AC-01
clarifications.observation: AC-03 (updated 2026-07-07) now says a boundary skip-back to 0:00 leaves the video in a PAUSED state, whereas a normal skip-back (AC-01) continues playback uninterrupted.
clarifications.consequence: Asymmetry: hitting the start boundary pauses, but a normal skip does not — may be an intended 'reached the start' behaviour or a copy of the end-of-video pause.
clarifications.question: Is pausing at 0:00 after a boundary skip-back intended, or should playback continue like AC-01? (AC-04 pausing at the final frame is expected; AC-03 pausing at 0:00 is the surprising one.)
clarifications.answer: Preserve the prior state on a skip-back that hits 0:00: if state=paused → stay paused; if state=playing → keep playing (continue from 0:00). Do not force a pause at the start boundary. (Decision from QA lead, 2026-07-08.)

resolution.rationale: Skip-back clamping to 0:00 must PRESERVE the prior playback state (playing→continue from 0:00; paused→stay paused), not force a pause — this makes AC-03 consistent with AC-01 (playing skip continues) and AC-05 (paused skip stays paused). Fixed UC3 AC-03 then[1]. The END boundary (AC-04) keeps 'end state (paused at final frame)' because reaching the final frame naturally ends playback (no content ahead) — so the asymmetry is now intentional and explained. Jira AC-03 still says 'paused state' → PM to align Jira (FU-5).
